column1: PROGRAM RULE: every test presented at a tollgate must report (1) the p-value, (2) the effect size with a confidence interval,
and (3) the pre-declared practical significance threshold. A result that is statistically significant but below the practical
threshold is reported as a NULL FINDING.
THREE ERRORS TO CHECK BEFORE EVERY TEST:
1. Testing before stratifying — aggregate comparisons are almost always contaminated by contact-mix shift. Run a chi-square first.
2. Treating agents as independent observations — contacts within an agent are correlated. Effective n is closer to the agent count.
3. Ignoring time-series structure — support data has strong day-of-week and intraday autocorrelation. Match day-of-week or use ITS.
TESTS REJECTED — record these so they are not re-litigated later
